status_summary: Executive Order 14148 of 2025-01-20 (90 FR 8237, published 2025-01-28) revoked Executive Order 14019 of 2021-03-07, Promoting Access to Voting, in section 2(aa). SBA's Administrator issued a memo published 2025-02-24 stating that SBA would end all taxpayer-funded voter registration activities, starting with rescinding its 2024 memorandum of understanding with the Michigan Secretary of State, and SBA's 100-day release of 2025-04-29 lists that memorandum as terminated. Executive Order 14248, signed 2025-03-25 and published 2025-03-28 (90 FR 14005), directs all agencies in section 9 to cease all actions implementing Executive Order 14019.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14148 (Initial Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions) revoked Executive Order 14019, published in the Federal Register on 2025-01-28.

SBA's Administrator issued a day-one priorities memo saying SBA would end all taxpayer-funded voter registration activities, starting with rescinding its 2024 memorandum of understanding with the Michigan Secretary of State.

Executive Order 14248, Preserving and Protecting the Integrity of American Elections, was signed (90 FR 14005, published 2025-03-28); section 9 directs agencies to cease all actions implementing Executive Order 14019 and to report on compliance within 90 days.
SBA's first 100 days release listed the 2024 memorandum of understanding with the Michigan Secretary of State as terminated.

title: End SBA's role as a designated voter registration agency under the 2021 voting order
uncertainties: The chapter lists SBA's request to become a designated voter agency as a concern rather than giving an explicit directive, so treating it as a recommendation to end that role is an inference. The only designation found is the 2024 Michigan memorandum; whether SBA had other state voter-registration arrangements was not checked, and the memorandum's terms were not read. The SBA releases describe the rescission in the agency's own words, and the 100-day release does not give the termination date. Litigation over Executive Order 14248 was reviewed on 2026-10-19: orders in the D.D.C. consolidated case (2026-03-31), the D. Mass. case (permanent injunction 2026-07-13) and the W.D. Wash. case (2026-01-09) address sections 2, 3, 4 and 7 and none discusses section 9 or Executive Order 14019. The 2026-03-31 D.D.C. order permanently enjoins SBA, among other agencies, from implementing section 2(d), which concerns citizenship checks by voter registration agencies; that is a different provision from section 9 and does not restore SBA's former registration role. The D.D.C. final judgment identifies the judge only by initials; appeals (First Circuit 25-01726 and a D.C. Circuit appeal of the section 2(a) judgment) were not tracked to a result. Orders were read through tracker or mirror copies hosted off the court sites.
